questions.sec: Ocular movements, refraction, accommodative squint and fusional vergence
questions.q: Per the book, ocular movements are examined in how many directions of gaze?
questions.exp: Examination of ocular movements: 9 directions of gaze, each with its acting muscle (1°, 2° and 3° gaze). (Book p48)

questions.sec: Ocular movements, refraction, accommodative squint and fusional vergence
questions.q: Match the gaze with its acting muscles in the book's 9-gaze figure — 1) Dextro-elevation 2) Sursumversion 3) Levo-depression … A) RSO + LIR B) RSR + RIO and LSR + LIO C) RSR + LIO
questions.exp: Dextro-elevation: RSR + LIO; sursumversion (B/L elevation): RSR + RIO and LSR + LIO; levo-depression: RSO + LIR. (Book p48)

questions.sec: Ocular movements, refraction, accommodative squint and fusional vergence
questions.q: Fill up: in the book's 9-gaze chart, dextroversion is achieved by ______.
questions.exp: Dextroversion: RLR + LMR; levoversion: RMR + LLR; deorsumversion: RIR + RSO and LIR + LSO. (Book p48)

questions.sec: Ocular movements, refraction, accommodative squint and fusional vergence
questions.q: Per the book, visual acuity <6/6 on Snellen's chart indicates a refractory error, measured by the:
questions.exp: Measurement of refractory error: visual acuity — Snellen's chart (6/6 normal; <6/6: refractory error → measured by retinoscope). (Book p48)

questions.sec: Ocular movements, refraction, accommodative squint and fusional vergence
questions.q: A 5-year-old with uncorrected hypermetropia develops an inward deviation. Per the book the chain is loss of near vision → overaccommodation + overconvergence → esotropia. The treatment listed is:
questions.exp: Accommodative squint: uncorrected hypermetropia → loss of near vision → overaccommodation + overconvergence → inward deviation: esotropia; treatment — use of spectacles. (Book p48)

questions.sec: Ocular movements, refraction, accommodative squint and fusional vergence
questions.q: Fill up: fusional vergence in the book is the extra power of the extraocular muscles to keep ______ from manifesting.
questions.exp: Fusional vergence: extra power of extraocular muscles to keep heterophoria from manifesting. (Book p48)

questions.sec: Ocular movements, refraction, accommodative squint and fusional vergence
questions.q: Among the book's tests for fusional vergence, the RAF (Royal Air Force) rule is the:
questions.exp: Tests for fusional vergence: Livingston gauge test, pencil test, synoptophore, RAF (Royal Air Force) rule — m/c used, a points measured. (Book p48)

questions.sec: Ocular movements, refraction, accommodative squint and fusional vergence
questions.q: Per the book's RAF ruler diagram, moving the ruler until the patient reports diplopia marks the near point of convergence, normal is ______; moving it until blurring marks the near point of accommodation (normal 20y: 8 cm, 50y: >46 cm).
questions.exp: RAF ruler (placed on nose): move until blurring → near point of accommodation (normal 20y — 8cm, 50y >46cm); move until diplopia → near point of convergence (normal <10 cm). (Book p48)

questions.sec: Measuring ocular deviation — objective tests (Hirschberg, Bruckner)
questions.q: Match the deviation-measurement group with its tests in the book — 1) Objective test 2) Subjective — ophthalmoplegic principle 3) Subjective — haploscope principle … A) Lancaster RG test, synoptophore B) Maddox rod, Maddox wing C) Hirschberg, Bruckner, cover-uncover, prism-bar cover
questions.exp: Objective: Hirschberg's, Bruckner's, cover-uncover, prism-bar cover. Subjective: based on the ophthalmoplegic principle — Maddox rod, Maddox wing; based on the haploscope principle — Lancaster RG test, synoptophore. (Book p49)

questions.sec: Measuring ocular deviation — objective tests (Hirschberg, Bruckner)
questions.q: The Hirschberg test in the book is also called the:
questions.exp: Hirschberg (corneal reflection) test: a. diagnosis of direction of deviation; b. measurement of degree of deviation. (Book p49)

questions.sec: Measuring ocular deviation — objective tests (Hirschberg, Bruckner)
questions.q: Fill up: for Hirschberg direction of deviation the book's mnemonic DOOR stands for deviation ______ of reflection.
questions.exp: Mnemonic: DOOR — deviation opposite of reflection (e.g. CR nasal to centre → 15° exodeviation at the pupillary margin). (Book p49)

questions.sec: Measuring ocular deviation — objective tests (Hirschberg, Bruckner)
questions.q: Per the book, 1 mm deviation of the corneal reflection from the centre of the pupil equals ______ of squint, i.e. 14 prism dioptres (1 pd = 1/2°).
questions.exp: Measurement of degree of deviation: 1 mm deviation of CR from centre of pupil = 7° squint / 14 prism dioptres; 1° = 2 pd (1 pd = 1/2°). (Book p49)

questions.sec: Measuring ocular deviation — objective tests (Hirschberg, Bruckner)
questions.q: In the book's photographic degree-deviation chart, the CR at the pupillary margin equals 15°/30 Δ and the CR at the limbus equals:
questions.exp: CR at pupillary margin = 15°/30 Δ; CR at limbus = 45°/90 Δ; the photograph series shows 15°, 30° and 45° for ESO and EXO (clinical rule HCRT). (Book p49)

questions.sec: Measuring ocular deviation — objective tests (Hirschberg, Bruckner)
questions.q: Per the book, Bruckner's test is a:
opts: Screening procedure in infants — examine the fundal red reflex
A subjective test for phoria at far fixation in adults
A test of stereopsis and depth perception
A test of colour vision in the pediatric age group
questions.exp: Bruckner's test: screening procedure in infants; shine light on the eye through direct ophthalmoscope; examine fundal red reflex. (Book p49)

questions.sec: Measuring ocular deviation — objective tests (Hirschberg, Bruckner)
questions.q: Match the Bruckner red reflex photograph finding with its interpretation in the book — 1) Equal reflex b/w both eyes 2) Arc-like reflex 3) Unequal reflex (R darker, L lighter) … A) Unequal squint B) Refracting error C) Normal red reflex
questions.exp: i. Red reflex: normal, equal b/w both eyes; ii. Arc-like reflex: refracting error; iii. Unequal squint (one darker, one lighter). (Book p50)

questions.sec: Cover–uncover test and the prism bar cover test
questions.q: Match the cover test with its purpose in the book — 1) Cover test 2) Uncover test … A) Diagnose phoria B) Confirm tropia
questions.exp: Cover test: confirm tropia; uncover test: diagnose phoria. (Book p50)

questions.sec: Cover–uncover test and the prism bar cover test
questions.q: Fill up: the book's mnemonic for the cover-uncover test, DOOM, stands for deviation ______ of movement.
questions.exp: Mnemonic: DOOM — deviation opposite of movement. (Book p50)

questions.sec: Cover–uncover test and the prism bar cover test
questions.q: In the book's uncover test diagram, on presentation there is no deviation on stress; the affected exophoric eye is covered, deviation appears under cover, and on removal the eye moves back to normal. This test is used to:
questions.exp: Uncover test: diagnose phoria — deviation under cover, movement of the eye back to normal on removal. (Book p50)

questions.sec: Cover–uncover test and the prism bar cover test
questions.q: The prism bar cover test (PBCT) in the book is the best and most accurate test for:
questions.exp: PBCT: best and most accurate test for the measurement of degree of tropia. (Book p50)

questions.sec: Cover–uncover test and the prism bar cover test
questions.q: Fill up: the PBCT principle is neutralization — light passing through a prism deviates towards the ______.
questions.exp: PBCT principle: neutralization → light passing through a prism deviates towards the apex; goal — finding the power of prism at which the eye appears normal on cover-uncover test. (Book p50)

questions.sec: Cover–uncover test and the prism bar cover test
questions.q: Match the deviation with the prism orientation during the test in the book — 1) ESO 2) EXO 3) Hyper 4) Hypo … A) Base-in prism B) Base-down prism C) Base-up prism D) Base-out prism
questions.exp: Orientation of prism: ESO — base out prism; EXO — base in prism; Hyper — base down prism; Hypo — base up prism. Mnemonic DOOB: deviation opposite of base of prism. (Book p50)

questions.sec: Cover–uncover test and the prism bar cover test
questions.q: The book's PBCT mnemonic DOOB (deviation opposite of base of prism) guides prism orientation. All of the following pairings are correct EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Hyper uses a base-DOWN prism (not base-up); hypo uses base-up. (Book p50)

questions.sec: Subjective tests (Maddox rod/wing) and diplopia
questions.q: Per the book, a use of the Maddox rod test is to measure/diagnose:
questions.exp: Maddox rod test uses: 1. measure/diagnose phoria at far fixation; 2. macular function test; 3. double Maddox rod test — measure cyclodeviation. (Book p51)

questions.sec: Subjective tests (Maddox rod/wing) and diplopia
questions.q: Match the Maddox rod result (patient's view) with the book's diagnosis — 1) Dot on the line 2) Left exophoria/tropia 3) Left esophoria/tropia … A) Orthophoria (normal) B) Crossed diplopia C) Uncrossed diplopia
questions.exp: Results: dot on the line — orthophoria (normal); left exophoria/tropia — crossed diplopia; left esophoria/tropia — uncrossed diplopia. (Book p51)

questions.sec: Subjective tests (Maddox rod/wing) and diplopia
questions.q: All of the following are stated about the Maddox wing in the book EXCEPT:
opts: It diagnoses phoria at near fixation
It is the most sensitive test for stereopsis
It is a subjective test based on the diplopia principle
questions.exp: Maddox wing: diagnoses phoria at near fixation; obsolete. It is not a stereopsis test. (Book p51)

questions.sec: Subjective tests (Maddox rod/wing) and diplopia
questions.q: Fill up: the book gives one test to differentiate between tropia and phoria: the ______.
questions.exp: Note: one test to differentiate between tropia and phoria — the cover-uncover test. (Book p51)

questions.sec: Subjective tests (Maddox rod/wing) and diplopia
questions.q: Monocular diplopia per the book is diplopia that does not disappear on closing the normal eye. Listed examples include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Monocular examples: subluxation of lens, severe refractory errors (anisometropia), iridodonesis; myasthenia gravis is a neuromuscular junction disorder causing BINOCULAR diplopia. (Book p51)

questions.sec: Subjective tests (Maddox rod/wing) and diplopia
questions.q: Match the binocular diplopia cause group with its example in the book — 1) Myogenic cause 2) Neurogenic 3) Neuromuscular junction disorders … A) Myasthenia gravis B) 3rd, 4th, 6th nerve palsy C) Squint d/t myogenic cause
questions.exp: Binocular diplopia disappears if either eye is closed; squint d/t: myogenic cause; neurogenic (3, 4, 6th nerve palsy); neuromuscular junction disorders (myasthenia gravis). (Book p51)

questions.sec: Subjective tests (Maddox rod/wing) and diplopia
questions.q: All of the following are listed diplopia tests in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Diplopia tests: red-green glasses (easiest way to check), Lee's screen, Hess chart (most commonly used). Amsler's grid is a retinal chart. (Book p51)

questions.sec: Subjective tests (Maddox rod/wing) and diplopia
questions.q: The easiest way to check for diplopia per the book is:
questions.exp: Red-green glasses: easiest way to check for diplopia; Hess chart: most commonly used for diplopia. (Book p51)

questions.sec: Sensory anomaly tests and stereopsis (G3 BSV)
questions.q: Match the sensory state with its meaning in the book — 1) BSV 2) ARC 3) Suppression … A) Adaptation to confusion B) 1 object 1 image C) Adaptation to diplopia
questions.exp: Tests for sensory anomalies differentiate: 1. BSV — 1 object 1 image; 2. ARC — adaptation to diplopia; 3. Suppression — adaptation to confusion. (Book p52)

questions.sec: Sensory anomaly tests and stereopsis (G3 BSV)
questions.q: Match the Worth 4-dot dots seen with the book's interpretation — 1) 4 dots 2) 5 dots 3) 3 dots (red not seen) 4) 2 dots (green not seen) … A) LE suppression B) Diplopia — non-harmonious ARC C) Normal BSV or harmonious ARC D) RE suppression (d/t amblyopia)
questions.exp: Worth 4-dot results: 4 dots — normal BSV/harmonious ARC; 5 dots — diplopia (non-harmonious ARC); 3 dots — RE suppression (d/t amblyopia); 2 dots — LE suppression. (Book p52)

questions.sec: Sensory anomaly tests and stereopsis (G3 BSV)
questions.q: Fill up: the book calls Worth's 4-dot test more common/more important than the ______ striated glasses test.
questions.exp: Worth's 4-dot test: more common/more important test > Bagolini striated glasses test. (Book p52)

questions.sec: Sensory anomaly tests and stereopsis (G3 BSV)
questions.q: Match the Worth 4-dot glass colour with the eye it is worn on in the book — 1) Red 2) Green … A) Worn on the right eye B) Worn on the left eye
questions.exp: Worth 4-dot method: red worn on the right eye; green worn on the left eye; 4 dots are shown. (Book p52)

questions.sec: Sensory anomaly tests and stereopsis (G3 BSV)
questions.q: Match the Bagolini striated glasses finding with the book's interpretation — 1) X (two crossing lines) 2) A single diagonal line 3) Two diverging lines … A) Diplopia — non-harmonious ARC B) Right eye suppression C) BSV or harmonious ARC
questions.exp: Bagolini results: X — binocular single vision or harmonious ARC; single line — right eye suppression; two diverging lines — diplopia, non-harmonious ARC. (Book p53)

questions.sec: Sensory anomaly tests and stereopsis (G3 BSV)
questions.q: The 4 prism test in the book is used to differentiate between BSV and ______ in microtropia (small angle squint).
questions.exp: 4 prism test: used to differentiate between BSV and central suppression scotoma in microtropia (small angle squint); the after image test is the other listed test. (Book p53)

questions.sec: Sensory anomaly tests and stereopsis (G3 BSV)
questions.q: All of the following are listed tests for stereopsis (G3 BSV, depth perception) in the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Stereopsis tests: 1. two pencil test (gross stereopsis); 2. Titmus fly test (Polaroid vectographic images, matte-ean grey); 3. random dot stereogram test — best test, eliminates monocular clues (Lang, Frisby, Frisby-Davis distance stereotest). (Book p53)

questions.sec: Sensory anomaly tests and stereopsis (G3 BSV)
questions.q: Which statement about the stereopsis tests is FALSE per the book?
opts: The Hess chart is the best test of stereopsis
The two pencil test assesses gross stereopsis
The Titmus fly test uses vectorographic images
The random dot stereogram test is the best test, used to eliminate monocular clues of depth perception
questions.exp: Best stereopsis test = random dot stereogram; the Hess chart is a diplopia chart (most commonly used for diplopia), not the best stereopsis test. (Book p53)

units.title: Ocular movements, refraction, accommodative squint and fusional vergence
units.guide: Examination of ocular movements: 9 directions of gaze — dextro-elevation (RSR + LIO), sursumversion (RSR + RIO, LSR + LIO), levo-elevation (RIO + LSR), dextroversion (RLR + LMR), primary position, levoversion (RMR + LLR), dextro-depression (RIR + LSO), deorsumversion (RIR + RSO, LIR + LSO), levo-depression (RSO + LIR). Refractory error: Snellen chart 6/6 normal; <6/6 → retinoscope. Accommodative squint: uncorrected hypermetropia → loss of near vision → overaccommodation + overconvergence → esotropia; treatment — spectacles. Fusional vergence: extra power of EOM to keep heterophoria from manifesting; tests — Livingston gauge, pencil, synoptophore, RAF rule (m/c used, a points measured); RAF ruler on nose: blurring point = near point of accommodation (normal 20y 8 cm, 50y >46 cm), diplopia point = near point of convergence (normal <10 cm); poor fusional vergence treated with orthoptic strengthening exercises.

units.title: Measuring ocular deviation — objective tests (Hirschberg, Bruckner)
units.guide: Objective tests: Hirschberg's, Bruckner's, cover-uncover, prism-bar cover. Subjective: ophthalmoplegic principle (Maddox rod, Maddox wing); haploscope principle (Lancaster RG, synoptophore). Hirschberg (corneal reflection): direction — DOOR (deviation opposite of reflection; CR nasal to centre → 15° exodeviation at pupillary margin); degree — 1 mm CR deviation = 7° squint/14 Δ (1 pd = 1/2°); CR at pupillary margin 15°/30 Δ, at limbus 45°/90 Δ (photographic chart 15/30/45°, clinical rule HCRT). Bruckner's: screening in infants; light through direct ophthalmoscope; examine fundal red reflex — equal b/w both eyes (normal), arc-like (refracting error), unequal (unequal squint).

units.title: Cover–uncover test and the prism bar cover test
units.guide: Cover test: confirm tropia (covered eye shows corrective movement); uncover test: diagnose phoria (deviation under cover, returns on removal). Mnemonic DOOM: deviation opposite of movement. PBCT: best and most accurate test for the measurement of degree of tropia; principle — neutralization, light through a prism deviates towards the apex; goal — prism power at which the eye appears normal on cover-uncover; mnemonic DOOB (deviation opposite of base of prism); orientation — ESO base-out, EXO base-in, hyper base-down, hypo base-up.

units.title: Subjective tests (Maddox rod/wing) and diplopia
units.guide: Maddox rod (diplopia principle): uses — measure/diagnose phoria at far fixation, macular function test, double Maddox rod test (measure cyclodeviation); results — dot on line: orthophoria; crossed diplopia: left exophoria/tropia; uncrossed: left esophoria/tropia. Maddox wing: diagnoses phoria at near fixation; obsolete. One test to differentiate tropia vs phoria: cover-uncover. Diplopia types: monocular (does not disappear on closing the normal eye — subluxation of lens, severe refractory errors/anisometropia, iridodonesis) and binocular (disappears if either eye is closed — squint d/t myogenic, neurogenic (3, 4, 6th nerve palsy), neuromuscular junction disorders (myasthenia gravis)). Tests: red-green glasses (easiest way), Lee's screen, Hess chart (most commonly used).

units.title: Sensory anomaly tests and stereopsis (G3 BSV, depth perception)
units.guide: Sensory anomaly tests differentiate: BSV (1 object 1 image), ARC (adaptation to diplopia), suppression (adaptation to confusion). Worth 4-dot: more common/more important > Bagolini; red on right eye, green on left eye; 4 dots — normal BSV/harmonious ARC; 5 dots — diplopia/non-harmonious ARC; 3 dots — RE suppression (d/t amblyopia); 2 dots — LE suppression. Bagolini striated glasses (RE 45°, LE 135°; light images perpendicular to striations): X — BSV or harmonious ARC; single line — RE suppression; diverging lines — diplopia, non-harmonious ARC. 4 prism test: differentiates BSV from central suppression scotoma in microtropia; after image test also listed. Stereopsis tests: two pencil (gross), Titmus fly (Polaroid vectographic), random dot stereogram — best (eliminates monocular clues): Lang, Frisby, Frisby-Davis distance stereotest.
